Hi Jared —

Appreciate the clear list. Short answers here and a set of artifacts attached for the SIG submission:

- Private endpoints vs VPC peering: Redwood supports both depending on deployment mode. For our hosted API (standard multi-tenant) we offer regionally-scoped static egress IP ranges that customers can allowlist; we do not enable VPC peering for multi-tenant hosted instances. For Dedicated and Private deployments we support either VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints). Recommendation: PrivateLink/interface endpoints for the smallest blast radius and to avoid cross-account routing changes — we note that peering is common for Dedicated when customers need full VPC-level integration.  

- Egress IPs: attached egress-ip-list.txt contains the current public egress CIDR blocks per region. For hosted customers these ranges are stable but subject to change with advance notice; we include an advisory clause in the SIG answer. For Dedicated/private we can provide fixed customer-dedicated NAT IPs when requested in the onboarding runbook.  

- Peering logs / audit: attaching vpc-peering-audit-20261120.csv (anonymized) as a sample. We can provide a fuller packet/flow audit under an NDA if needed for procurement/security review.  

- Suggested SIG wording: see the 'SIG-answers-network-section.xlsx' tab 'Network - draft' (attached) — it contains short, audit-ready phrasing with control IDs mapped to the SIG v3.0 rows.

Attachments: [redwood-sig-network-diagram.pdf] [SIG-answers-network-section.xlsx] [egress-ip-list.txt] [vpc-peering-audit-20261120.csv]

If you'd like, I can update the SIG spreadsheet with your exact control text and re-send. Also cc'ing our security lead for a quick technical confirmation.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
